UK STATUTORY RESIDENCE TEST CHECKER · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER · NOTHING UPLOADED

Are you UK resident this tax year, and how many more UK days can you spend?

List your UK stays, answer a few questions about your home, work and family, and see which part of the Statutory Residence Test decides: the automatic overseas tests, the automatic UK tests, or the sufficient ties test. You also get the number of days that would flip the answer.

Written from the published test without a live lookup. HMRC and the courts decide residence; split-year treatment and the deeming rule are not modelled. Not tax advice.

What it does, and what it leaves to you

    
    
      
  • Covers: the three automatic overseas tests, the three automatic UK tests and the sufficient ties test for leavers and arrivers, with days counted as midnights, overlapping stays merged and up to 60 exceptional days removed.
    • 
      
  • Gives: the test that decided and why, the ties present against the number needed, and the days of headroom (or the days to cut) that change the answer. The full threshold table is in the ties table guide.
    • 
      
  • Not decided: split-year treatment, the deeming rule, deaths in the year, Crown and forces employees, domicile and the remittance basis, double tax treaty tie-breakers, and whether a particular home or work pattern meets HMRC's wording. You answer those questions; HMRC or an adviser decides them.
    • 
    

  


  

    
Common questions

    
What is the UK Statutory Residence Test?

    
A three-part test that decides whether you are UK resident for a tax year (6 April to 5 April). First the automatic overseas tests, then the automatic UK tests, and if neither settles it, the sufficient ties test, which compares your days in the UK against the ties you keep here.

    
Is the 183-day rule the whole test?

    
No. 183 days or more in the UK makes you resident, but you can be resident on far fewer days: with a UK home, a UK-resident family, work here and days from earlier years, as few as 16 days can be enough for someone who recently left.

    
What counts as a day in the UK?

    
A day you are in the UK at midnight at the end of it. Arriving on the 10th and leaving on the 15th is 5 days. Passing through on the same day, or being in transit, is generally not a day. Up to 60 days of exceptional circumstances can be left out.

    
What is the difference between a leaver and an arriver?

    
A leaver was UK resident in at least one of the previous three tax years; an arriver was not. Leavers have five possible ties (including the country tie) and a stricter table; arrivers have four.

    
Does this decide whether I am UK resident?

    
No. It runs the published test on the dates and answers you type and shows which step decided. It does not model split-year treatment, the deeming rule or deaths in the year. Check HMRC's RDR3 guidance or an adviser.

    
Is my data uploaded anywhere?

    
No. Everything is calculated in your browser and nothing is sent.

  

  

    
No warranty. This tool is provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied. It is not tax, legal, or immigration advice and does not decide anyone's tax residence. You are responsible for checking its output against HMRC's guidance (RDR3, the Statutory Residence Test) or a qualified adviser before relying on it.

    
Your answers. This page runs in your browser and sends nothing anywhere; closing the tab discards them, and downloads are files on your own device.

    
Best-effort hosting, no SLA. These tools are free, experimental, and may be slow, broken, moved, or taken offline without notice. We do not promise uptime, backups of anything you type, or that a URL will keep working. Do not use this as a system of record: nothing you enter is saved anywhere.

    
Everything runs in your browser. Your answers are never uploaded; there are no accounts, cookies, or analytics vendors. Anonymous feature events (analysis_run, example_loaded, summary_downloaded) are counted only in local storage on your device, never with any of your data, and are switched off by Do Not Track.

UK Statutory Residence Test checker · guide

UK Statutory Residence Test ties table: how many days with how many ties

If no automatic overseas test and no automatic UK test settles your residence for the tax year, the sufficient ties test does. It compares the days you spent in the UK with the number of ties you keep here. Which table applies depends on whether you were UK resident in any of the previous three tax years.

Leavers: UK resident in one or more of the last 3 tax years

Five ties can count: family, accommodation, work, 90-day and country.

Days in the UKResult
0 to 15Automatically not resident
16 to 45Resident with 4 or more ties
46 to 90Resident with 3 or more ties
91 to 120Resident with 2 or more ties
121 to 182Resident with 1 or more ties
183 or moreAutomatically resident

Arrivers: not UK resident in any of the last 3 tax years

Four ties can count: the country tie does not apply.

Days in the UKResult
0 to 45Automatically not resident
46 to 90Resident with 4 or more ties
91 to 120Resident with 3 or more ties
121 to 182Resident with 2 or more ties
183 or moreAutomatically resident

The ties

  • Family: a spouse, civil partner or partner you live with who is UK resident, or a child under 18 who is UK resident and whom you see in the UK on at least 61 days.
  • Accommodation: a place to live available for a continuous 91 days or more in the tax year, where you spend at least one night (16 nights if it belongs to a close relative).
  • Work: three or more hours of work in the UK on at least 40 days in the tax year.
  • 90-day: 90 or more days in the UK in either of the previous two tax years.
  • Country (leavers only): you spent more days in the UK than in any other single country.

Worked example

A recent leaver spends 101 days in the UK in 2026/27. They keep a family tie and an accommodation tie, so 2 ties. At 101 days a leaver needs 2, so they are resident under this test. At 90 days the requirement is 3, so they would not be: 11 fewer days changes the answer. Try your own numbers.

Common questions

How many days can I spend in the UK without becoming resident?

It depends on your ties. With no ties, up to 182 days; a recent leaver with four ties becomes resident at 16 days; an arriver with all four ties becomes resident at 46. The tables on this page give the threshold for every number of days.

What are the five ties?

Family, accommodation, work, 90-day and (for leavers only) country. Each is defined in HMRC's RDR3 guidance; the checker asks you a question for each.

No warranty. Free and as-is; not tax, legal, or immigration advice. The table is written from HMRC's published Statutory Residence Test guidance (RDR3) without a live lookup. Check it against the current guidance before relying on it. Automatic tests, split-year treatment and the deeming rule can override the table.

Everything runs in your browser. Nothing you type is uploaded.
